title: Z80 CPU memory, I/O ports and video memory
summary: The X1 uses separate 16-bit Z80 CPU-memory and I/O-port spaces. Text and graphics VRAM are reached through I/O ports, not by changing the CPU-memory bank.
syntax: IN A,(C) / OUT (C),A                 16-bit I/O port in BC
notes: CPU addresses and I/O ports both range from 0000H through FFFFH, but they are independent namespaces. The same numeric value does not identify the same storage.
X1 text VRAM is decoded at I/O ports 2000H through 3FFFH and graphics VRAM at 4000H through FFFFH. These are not CPU-memory addresses.
x1pen_debug_read_memory observes the Z80's currently mapped 64KB CPU view. Use x1pen_debug_read_vram for text, attribute, kanji or graphics video memory.
Do not invent a CPU bank switch to reach VRAM. X1turbo low-memory banks and graphics VRAM banks are separate mechanisms.
A general debugger IN/OUT API is intentionally not exposed: device reads can acknowledge interrupts, consume data or change modes. VRAM debugger reads use a side-effect-free physical view.
On this X1 implementation, every ordinary IN clears graphics simultaneous-access mode. A debugger VRAM read does not call Z80_In and therefore does not clear it.

examples.title: Read and write a 16-bit X1 I/O port through BC
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,04000H
IN A,(C)
OUT (C),A
RET

title: CPU memory map and X1turbo low-memory banks
summary: CPU addresses 8000H-FFFFH always use main RAM. The 0000H-7FFFH view can select IPL ROM/main RAM, and X1turbo/Z can instead map one of sixteen 32KB bank-RAM pages.
syntax: A bit 4 = 0     map bank RAM page A bits 3..0 to 0000H-7FFFH
A bit 4 = 1     use normal IPL-ROM/main-RAM low-memory mapping
OUT (1D00H),A   enable IPL ROM reads in normal mapping
OUT (1E00H),A   enable main RAM reads in normal mapping
notes: The 0Bxx selector and sixteen 32KB bank pages are available only on X1turbo and X1turboZ. Original X1 does not provide this bank-RAM mapping.
In normal low-memory mapping, writes go to main RAM. Reads select IPL ROM or main RAM according to the ROM switch controlled by 1Dxx and 1Exx output ports.
The debugger state reports lowMemory.mapping as bios, main or bank and reports the selected bank when applicable. x1pen_debug_read_memory follows that active view.
Graphics bank 0/1 is unrelated to these CPU-memory pages. Select graphics banks only through screen control or the VRAM debugger bank parameter.
EMM is a separate I/O peripheral and is not the X1turbo low-memory bank mechanism. See x1.io.emm-rom for its independent address/data ports.

examples.title: Write turbo bank-RAM page 2 from stable high memory
examples.source:
ORG 8000H
LD BC,00B00H
LD A,02H
OUT (C),A
LD HL,0000H
LD (HL),05AH
LD A,010H
OUT (C),A
RET

title: Text, attribute and kanji VRAM
summary: Text display uses three logical 2048-byte regions in I/O space: attributes at canonical 2000H-27FFH, ANK character codes at 3000H-37FFH, and turbo/Z kanji codes at 3800H-3FFFH.
syntax: 3800H-3FFFH   kanji-code VRAM on turbo/Z; ANK mirror on X1
notes: Each debugger region uses logical offsets 0000H-07FFH. Use region text, attribute or kanji instead of passing an I/O port as the offset.
The canonical attribute range is 2000H-27FFH. 2800H-2FFFH is a mirror alias of the same 2048 bytes.
On original X1, hardware reads and writes at 3800H-3FFFH mirror ANK text VRAM. Software can use this behavior to distinguish X1 from turbo models.
The debugger deliberately rejects region kanji on original X1 so clients do not mistake the mirror for an independent region. Read region text to observe the underlying ANK data.
Writing through the debugger applies the emulator's normal text dirty, blink and double-size handling and is allowed only while paused.

examples.title: Put a white A in the first text cell
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,01A02H
IN A,(C)
LD BC,03000H
LD A,041H
OUT (C),A
LD BC,02000H
LD A,07H
OUT (C),A
RET

title: Graphics VRAM banks, color planes and simultaneous access
summary: Graphics VRAM has independent blue, red and green 16KB planes. X1turbo/Z provides banks 0 and 1, while original X1 supports bank 0 only.
syntax: 4000H-7FFFH   BLUE plane in normal single-plane mode
8000H-BFFFH   RED plane in normal single-plane mode
C000H-FFFFH   GREEN plane in normal single-plane mode
notes: Normal plane accesses use the low 14 port bits as a logical offset 0000H-3FFFH. The debugger exposes this contiguous offset and hides GRP_RAM's internal interleaving.
Bank 1 is available only on X1turbo and X1turboZ. Original X1 rejects debugger requests for bank 1.
The current display bank and CPU access bank are separate. MCP accepts numeric bank 0/1 or the selectors display/access and returns the resolved numeric bank.

PPI port C at 1A02H controls the simultaneous-access trigger. A bit-5 falling edge enters the mode; subsequent OUT instructions write the plane combinations shown above instead of ordinary I/O devices.
Any ordinary IN clears simultaneous-access mode. x1pen_debug_read_vram does not perform IN and therefore does not disturb the mode.
Pause before a multi-byte dump when a consistent snapshot matters. Debugger writes are paused-only and mark changed graphics bytes for a later display frame.

examples.title: Write one byte to the blue graphics plane
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,01A02H
IN A,(C)
LD BC,04000H
LD A,080H
OUT (C),A
RET

title: Screen control, CRTC and graphics bank selection
aliases: 表示バンク アクセスバンク
summary: The CRTC and PPI determine text and graphics dimensions. X1turbo/Z screen-control port 1FD0H also selects the displayed and CPU-access graphics banks independently.
syntax: 1A02H         PPI port C; bit 6 reflects/selects 40 versus 80 columns
notes: Port 1FD0H and graphics bank 1 require X1turbo or X1turboZ. Original X1 has one graphics bank.
Display bank controls what the video hardware shows. Access bank controls which graphics bank ordinary I/O reads and writes reach. They may intentionally differ for page flipping.
x1pen_debug_get_video_state returns the raw screenBits plus resolved displayBank/accessBank and dimensions derived by the emulator's current CRTC state.
Do not recompute the current dimensions from screenBits alone; CRTC registers and the 40/80-column PPI state also contribute.
The MCP VRAM display/access selectors are resolved inside the same WASM call as the copy, avoiding a bank-change race within the single-threaded emulator call.

examples.title: Toggle the displayed graphics bank on X1turbo/Z
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,01FD0H
IN A,(C)
XOR 08H
OUT (C),A
RET

title: PCG character patterns and base graphics palette
aliases: キャラクタジェネレータ
summary: PCG provides blue, red and green pattern bytes for programmable text characters. Base graphics palette components are controlled through the 1000H, 1100H and 1200H port groups.
syntax: attribute bit 5 (20H) selects PCG for a text cell
notes: A PCG glyph is color-planar: each raster row has separate blue, red and green pattern bytes. The text attribute PCG bit selects programmable rather than ROM character data.
Original-compatible PCG access is synchronized with the currently scanned text cell. X1turbo/Z high-speed PCG mode changes addressing behavior and is selected by screen-control bit 5.
Direct PCG port programming is timing- and mode-sensitive. For FuzzyBASIC or SLANG, prefer the bundled PCG helpers documented by those language profiles unless hardware-level control is required.
The 1000H/1100H/1200H groups are base blue/red/green palette controls. The 1300H group controls display priority. X1turboZ extended modes are documented separately.
PCG RAM is not exposed by the current VRAM debugger regions. text and attribute regions let a debugger inspect which character and PCG attribute a cell uses.

examples.title: Set the base blue palette component
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,01000H
LD A,0FFH
OUT (C),A
RET

title: X millennium Web implemented I/O port map
summary: Complete routing overview for I/O devices implemented by the current X millennium Web build; use the related dedicated entry for register semantics and side effects.
syntax: 0BxxH turbo low-memory selector; 0DxxH EMM; 0ExxH ROM board and kanji ROM
1FD0H/1FE0H turbo/Z screen and black control; 1FF0H-1FFFH DIP switch
notes: This map follows Z80_In and Z80_Out in the current emulator, not a union of every expansion ever sold for X1.
Port decoding often uses only the high byte or masked low bits, so aliases exist. Dedicated entries identify canonical ports and the exact aliases used by this implementation.
An active PPI simultaneous-access mode intercepts every OUT before normal device decoding. Every ordinary IN clears that mode before reading its target device.
Some ranges are model- or option-dependent. Check each dedicated entry before emitting code for original X1, X1turbo or X1turboZ.
General debugger IN/OUT remains intentionally unavailable because reads and writes can acknowledge interrupts, advance FIFOs, change disk handshakes or alter display modes.

examples.title: Read the PPI status port using a 16-bit I/O address
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,01A01H
IN A,(C)
RET

title: 8255 PPI, sub CPU, keyboard, calendar and cassette commands
summary: Port 1900H exchanges command/data bytes with the X1 sub CPU, while PPI ports 1A00H-1A03H expose handshake, display, ROM and simultaneous-graphics control signals.
syntax: 1A01H       PPI port B status: bit7 display, bit6 sub busy, bit5 output empty, bit4 RAM view, bit2 V-SYNC
1A02H       PPI port C: bit6 40/80-column state; bit5 falling edge enters simultaneous graphics mode
D0H-D7H     write six-byte timer slot 0-7; D8H-DFH read six-byte timer slot 0-7
E3H game keys; E4H keyboard IRQ vector; E6H key data; E7H/E8H TV control
E9H-EFH cassette status/sensor and three-byte calendar/time set/get
notes: Sub-CPU traffic is handshaked through PPI status. Do not stream command and data bytes without observing buffer state.
Reading 1900H consumes the currently presented sub-CPU output byte. Keyboard interrupts also fetch their vector through this path.
The emulator implements E3/E4/E6-EF and D0-DF behavior used for game keys, keyboard, cassette, calendar, clock and timers; unsupported command values have no useful contract.
PPI port B and port C contain live status. Reads are not passive snapshots because every IN also clears graphics simultaneous-access mode.
Use language/runtime keyboard and file helpers when possible; use this protocol only for hardware-level software.

examples.title: Read PPI handshake and display status
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,01A01H
IN A,(C)
RET

title: AY-3-8910 PSG and joystick ports
aliases: ジョイスティック ビット割り当て
summary: Select an AY-3-8910 register through the 1CxxH group, then read or write it through the 1BxxH group; input registers 14 and 15 carry joystick-style data.
syntax: IN  1BxxH           read selected register or joystick input
registers 0-5 tone, 6 noise, 7 mixer/I/O, 8-10 volume, 11-13 envelope, 14-15 I/O
PSG clock = 2,000,000 Hz; tone period = clock / (16 * frequency)
notes: Use BC with OUT (C),A and IN A,(C); the X1 decodes the 16-bit port high byte, not only an 8-bit immediate port.

The AY-3-8910 receives a 2 MHz clock. Round clock / (16 * frequency) to the nearest supported 12-bit tone period. For channel A, A4 at 440 Hz uses period 284 (011CH): register 0 (fine) = 1CH and register 1 (coarse) = 01H, producing about 440.14 Hz. The coarse register uses only its low four bits, so tone periods are limited to 12 bits.

The bit table applies identically to raw bytes read from register 14 or 15. The Web emulator combines physical gamepad state into register 14 and applies JoyKey keyboard mapping to register 14 or 15 according to Key Mode.
Buttons 3 and 4 are additional mappings exposed by the Web emulator platform layer; do not assume that a physical two-button X1 pad drives those lines.
Joystick bits are active-low: 0 means pressed, and 255 (FFH) means that no direction or button is pressed.
For successive raw samples, (NEW XOR OLD) AND OLD yields the newly pressed bits. For example, OLD=FFH and NEW=FEH produces 01H for a new Up press.
Writes to registers 14 and 15 are not modeled as general-purpose output by this implementation.
For FuzzyBASIC or SLANG music playback, prefer their documented PSG drivers unless direct tone-register control is required.

examples.title: Read joystick input from PSG register 14
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,01C00H
LD A,0EH
OUT (C),A
LD BC,01B00H
IN A,(C)
RET

examples.title: Detect newly pressed active-low joystick bits
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
; B=OLD, A=NEW
XOR B
AND B
RET

title: YM2151 OPM sound-board ports
summary: The optional YM2151-compatible OPM board uses 0700H for register selection and 0701H for register data; reads return board-presence/status behavior.
notes: The OPM board is optional and controlled by the emulator sound-board setting. Status reads return 00H when enabled and FFH when absent in this implementation.
Direct YM2151 programming requires the chip register contract in addition to this X1 port map.
The adjacent 0704H-0707H range is the sound-board CTC, not OPM register data.

examples.title: Silence OPM channel 0 by writing key-off register 08H
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,00700H
LD A,08H
OUT (C),A
INC C
XOR A
OUT (C),A
RET

title: Z80 CTC timers and interrupt vectors
summary: X1turbo/Z exposes two four-channel CTC blocks at 1FA0H and 1FA8H; an enabled OPM board adds a third block at 0704H.
syntax: write control/vector then optional time constant; read current down-counter
notes: The 1FAxH blocks require X1turbo or X1turboZ. The 0704H block is present only when the sound-board option is enabled.
This implementation follows the Z80 CTC control-word protocol and IM 2 vector generation; consult the Z80 CTC programming model for control-bit details.
Channels 1 and 2 use a 2MHz source in counter mode, channel 3 may cascade from channel 0, and timer timing is based on a fixed 4MHz source in the emulator.
Reading a channel returns its current counter and every IN clears graphics simultaneous-access mode.

examples.title: Read turbo CTC block 0 channel 1
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,01FA1H
IN A,(C)
RET

title: X1turbo Z80 DMA command stream
aliases: ダイレクトメモリアクセス
summary: X1turbo/Z routes 1F80H-1F8FH to one Z80 DMA command/status stream used with peripherals such as the FDC and SASI interface.
syntax: 1F80H-1F8FH write = Z80 DMA WR0-WR6 command/parameter byte stream
1F80H-1F8FH read = status or bytes selected by read-mask command
notes: All sixteen decoded addresses reach the same command-stream parser; they are aliases, not sixteen independent DMA registers.
The command byte determines which parameter bytes follow. Do not treat later bytes as fixed port offsets.
The emulator models address A/B, byte count, search/match, READY, interrupt and RETI behavior. FDC and SASI update DMA READY during transfers.
DMA ports require X1turbo or X1turboZ. Use the Z80 DMA programming contract when constructing WR0-WR6 sequences.

examples.title: Read current DMA status
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,01F80H
IN A,(C)
RET

title: Z80 SIO channels and X1 mouse packet
summary: Ports 1F90H-1F93H expose two Z80 SIO channels; the current Web implementation feeds a three-byte X1 mouse packet into channel B when RTS rises.
syntax: mouse packet = buttons/overflow flags, signed X delta, signed Y delta
notes: Even ports are data and odd ports are control/status. Select SIO write/read registers through the channel control port according to the Z80 SIO protocol.
On channel B, a rising RTS bit in WR5 requests a fresh three-byte mouse packet. The first byte contains two button bits and X/Y overflow flags.
The receive data port consumes queued bytes and may clear receive interrupt state; it is not a passive debugger read.
The current X1_IO decoder does not apply a ROM_TYPE guard to 1F90H-1F93H, although software normally associates this interface with turbo-class hardware.

examples.title: Read SIO channel B status register zero
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,01F93H
IN A,(C)
RET

title: Floppy disk controller, drive and media ports
summary: The X1 FDC uses 0FF8H-0FFBH for command/status, track, sector and data, 0FFCH for drive/side/motor selection, and read strobes at 0FFEH/0FFFH for media rate.
syntax: 0FF9H track register; 0FFAH sector register; 0FFBH data register
0FFCH write: bits 1..0 drive, bit4 side, bit7 motor
0FFEH read selects 1.6M media timing; 0FFFH read selects 500K/1M timing
notes: Command high nibbles follow the WD17xx-style restore, seek, step, read/write sector, read address, force interrupt and track operations modeled in X1_fdc.cpp.
Reading or writing the data register advances an active transfer and changes FDC/DMA handshake state. Never poll it as a harmless presence test.
The Web emulator connects mounted D88 and 2D images to this controller. The browser file-management API is separate from guest-visible FDC ports.
Drive select values 0-3 address the four emulated drives; motor and side are part of the same 0FFCH byte.

examples.title: Read FDC status
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,00FF8H
IN A,(C)
RET

title: SASI hard-disk interface and handshake phases
summary: Ports 0FD0H-0FD3H implement the X1 SASI data, control, reset and selection handshake used by mounted SASI disk images.
syntax: 0FD1H read control signals; write deasserts selection
0FD3H write asserts selection with target value
status bits: bit0 REQ, bit1 BSY, bit2 I/O, bit3 C/D, bit4 MSG
notes: Data-port access advances the current SASI command/data/status/message phase. Poll 0FD1H for REQ and phase bits before transferring data.
REQ also drives the emulated DMA READY signal, allowing the Z80 DMA block to transfer SASI data.
The implemented command set is the subset handled by X1_sasi.cpp and 256-byte image sectors; do not infer later SCSI commands.
This interface is compiled into the current Web build through T_TUNE=1.

examples.title: Read SASI control signals without consuming data
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,00FD1H
IN A,(C)
RET

title: EMM slots and ROM BASIC board sequential ports
summary: Ten file-backed EMM slots use four-port address/data windows beginning at 0D00H; the 0ExxH ROM BASIC board exposes a separate 24-bit sequential read address.
syntax: base+0 low address, base+1 middle address, base+2 high address, base+3 data with auto-increment
ROM board 0ExxH low two bits: 0=high address, 1=middle, 2=low, 3=data read
0E80H-0E83H is intercepted by the kanji-ROM interface before ROM-board decoding
notes: EMM is an I/O peripheral and is unrelated to X1turbo low-memory bank RAM or graphics VRAM banks.
Reading or writing an EMM data port increments that slot's 24-bit address. Writes are persisted to the browser-managed EMM image through the emulator cache.
Only slots 0-9 are implemented even though the high-byte decoder covers 0D00H-0DFFH; later four-byte windows return FFH or ignore writes.
The ROM board read path is backed by ROMBASIC.ROM. Address programming order differs from EMM and data reads do not auto-increment in the current implementation.
The 0E80H kanji range has priority over the ROM board and must not be used as a ROM BASIC address window.

examples.title: Read one byte from EMM0 address 001234H
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,00D00H
LD A,34H
OUT (C),A
INC C
LD A,12H
OUT (C),A
INC C
XOR A
OUT (C),A
INC C
IN A,(C)
RET

title: Kanji ROM code and raster data ports
summary: Ports 0E80H and 0E81H hold the X1 kanji code and return left/right raster bytes; writing 0E82H latches the selected glyph in the current implementation.
syntax: IN 0E80H = left raster; IN 0E81H = right raster; reading both advances row 0-15
notes: The interface returns 16 rows of two bytes. The row advances only after both left and right bytes have been read.
Code conversion follows the X1 kanji-ROM address/JIS mapping implemented by adr2jis_x1 and jis2adr_x1.
0E80H-0E83H is decoded before the broader 0ExxH ROM BASIC board range.
This kanji ROM interface is distinct from the text-screen kanji VRAM at 3800H-3FFFH.

examples.title: Select a kanji code and read the first raster pair
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,00E80H
LD A,21H
OUT (C),A
INC C
LD A,21H
OUT (C),A
INC C
XOR A
OUT (C),A
DEC C
DEC C
IN A,(C)
INC C
IN A,(C)
RET

title: X1turboZ analog palette and extended display controls
summary: X1turboZ adds analog/4096-color palette modes and extended text/graphics controls at 1FB0H-1FC5H; turbo-class screen and DIP controls occupy 1FD0H-1FFFH.
syntax: 1FC0H extended text display/priority; 1FC5H extended graphics palette control
1FF0H-1FFFH read DIP switch value on turbo/Z
notes: The 1FB0H, 1FB9H-1FBFH, 1FC0H and 1FC5H controls require X1turboZ. Do not emit them for original X1 or X1turbo.
Extended palette mode changes how 1000H-12FFH palette writes are decoded, including 64-color and 4096-color indexing. Program the mode before component values.
Port 1FE0H writes black control on turbo/Z in this emulator, but readback is exposed only for turboZ by the current decoder.
DIP switch bit 0 selects the startup resolution family and bit 2 selects boot media; 1FF0H-1FFFH are aliases returning the same byte.
Use x1pen_debug_get_video_state for current dimensions and graphics banks; it does not expose the full analog palette register set.

examples.title: Read the X1turboZ extended palette mode
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD BC,01FB0H
IN A,(C)
RET
